elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Sections 2.1 and 2.2 expressly grant the licences to Corio and its Affiliates, supported by an operative Affiliate definition.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Sections 2.1 and 2.2 expressly grant the licences to contractors acting on Corio's behalf.
Section 2.2 describes the Internal Use License as both fully paid up and perpetual.
Section 2.2's fully paid-up licence is not stated to be irrevocable. The irrevocability language appears only in Section 2.1, whose licence is fee-bearing rather than fully paid up.

elements.element: Subscription licences may be terminated only for material breach.
elements.evidence: The rendered provisions contain no subscription licence: Section 2.1 is expressly perpetual, and Section 2.2 is fully paid up and perpetual. The condition triggering this requirement is therefore demonstrably absent from the supplied licence provisions.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated for material breach only if that breach remains uncured.
elements.evidence: The rendered provisions contain no subscription licence: both supplied licences are expressly perpetual, and Section 2.2 is also fully paid up. The condition triggering this requirement is therefore demonstrably absent.

elements.element: The licences are transferable to successors.
elements.evidence: Sections 2.1 and 2.2 remain expressly nontransferable except under Section 14.1. Section 14.1 permits certain M&A assignments but requires consent when the transaction involves the other party's direct competitor; its successors language applies only subject to those restrictions.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered by the licence upon written notice to the licensor.
elements.evidence: Sections 2.1 and 2.2 provide stronger, automatic affiliate coverage without requiring notice. Accordingly, affiliates remain covered if written notice is given.

elements.element: The licences are transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 generally permits assignment in connection with a merger, acquisition, or relevant asset sale, but requires the other party's consent if the transaction involves its direct competitor. The unqualified fallback transfer right is therefore not fully provided.

result.reason: The redline successfully adds automatic affiliate and contractor coverage and preserves the perpetual character of the fully paid-up licence. It does not make that paid-up licence irrevocable and does not provide an unrestricted successor-transfer right. The M&A assignment right remains subject to a competitor-consent exception, so the fallback is also incomplete. The added CUSTOMER(S) definition is unrelated to the requested licence-scope changes and may alter other commercial provisions; it is also grammatically inconsistent ('customers ... its ... who obtains').
